attribution.note: Marcus's own words in his post's P.S., stated as fact.

semantics.note: The proposition matches the firm statement that Character.AI has filed for bankruptcy. The CoreWeave clause is handled separately.

contract.note: Treating the brand as its operating company and requiring a filing by the post date is the ordinary reading. It does not require a shutdown.

evidence.note: Company announcement dated Oct 12 saying Character.ai began a voluntary Chapter 11 process. This is a company disclosure, but it is consistent with e2.
US Trustee notice dated Oct 13 names the debtor, Character Technologies, Inc., case 26-11603 (BLS), D. Del. It confirms a voluntary petition existed before the post.

reviews.rationale: An official US Trustee notice dated Oct 13, 2026 confirms that Character Technologies, Inc. filed a Chapter 11 petition in Delaware. The company's Oct 12 announcement agrees. Both predate the Oct 14 post, and the packet has no counterevidence.

attribution.note: Marcus's own words in his P.S. The embedded tweet is context, not his claim.

semantics.note: The firm part is that CoreWeave bonds reached 15%. The 'suggesting' inference is kept as hedged and is not scored.

contract.note: Reading 15% as a secondary-market yield, allowing any issue, ordinary rounding and an intraday high over Oct 13-14 is the reading an informed reader would take. The hedged inference is correctly left unscored.

evidence.note: Benzinga, Oct 14: the 2032 bonds touched a 15% intraday yield on Oct 13 and closed at 14.5%. It relies on an investor's chart, not primary trade records.
Secondary summary citing FINRA TRACE: the 2031 notes yielded 14.7% at end of day on Oct 13. That is about 15% at whole-percent precision.

reviews.rationale: Two independent dated sources put CoreWeave bond yields at about 15% on Oct 13, 2026: a 15% intraday high on the 2032s and a 14.7% end-of-day yield on the 2031s. This meets the contract. The 'credit markets have had enough' inference is hedged and is not scored.
